findings.title: confirm() blocks forever when stdin is closed; no TTY guard on profile delete
findings.detail: profile_delete.go:confirm() calls bufio.NewReader(cmd.InOrStdin()).ReadString('\n'). When an agent runs this command without --yes and stdin is /dev/null or a closed pipe, ReadString blocks until EOF then returns err != nil, which causes confirm() to return false — silently cancelling instead of failing. The agent sees exit code 0 and output 'Cancelled.' with no error, making it impossible to distinguish a successful confirm-skip from a hung or refused operation. The --yes/-y flag exists and bypasses this correctly, but it is not documented in the Short description and nothing in the command's help text flags it as required for non-interactive use.
findings.suggested_fix: 1. Add a TTY check: if !isatty.IsTerminal(os.Stdin.Fd()) && !yes { return fmt.Errorf("stdin is not a TTY; re-run with --yes to confirm deletion") }. 2. Add 'requires --yes in non-interactive contexts' to the command Long description. 3. Use the github.com/mattn/go-isatty package (already common in Cobra CLIs) or the os.ModeCharDevice check. Cobra-idiomatic pattern: set a persistent pre-run hook on the root that exports an IsTerminal bool into a context, then consume it in mutating commands.

findings.title: All failures collapse to exit code 1; agents cannot distinguish not-found vs already-exists vs lock contention
findings.detail: main.go calls os.Exit(1) for every error returned from Execute(). The profile package defines ErrAlreadyExists and ErrNotFound as sentinel errors (manager.go:23-26), and fslock.Acquire can block or fail. None of these produce distinct exit codes. An agent retrying 'ccp profile create foo' after a transient failure has no way to know whether exit 1 means 'profile already exists (stop retrying)' vs 'lock timeout (retry is safe)' vs 'disk full (escalate)'. The domain already has the right sentinel errors; they are just never surfaced as codes.

evidence.also: /Users/dalley/dev/Personal/ccp/internal/profile/manager.go lines 23-26: ErrAlreadyExists, ErrNotFound defined but not mapped to exit codes

findings.suggested_fix: Define an exit-code map in main.go using errors.Is: ErrNotFound->2, ErrAlreadyExists->3, lock errors->4 (retryable). Cobra supports this by returning a *cobra.Command exit code via cmd.ExecuteC() and inspecting the returned error before calling os.Exit. Document the codes in --help text or a man page. This is the same pattern used by git (128=not a git repo, 1=generic, 2=merge conflict) and docker (125/126/127 for container vs exec failures).

findings.title: Data-returning commands lack --json: show, diff, doctor, sync status, version, current
findings.command: ccp profile show / diff / doctor / sync status / version / current
findings.detail: profile list has --json (profile_list.go:44) and emitListJSON, but the six other data-returning commands emit only prose. An agent consuming 'ccp profile show work' must parse lines like 'Source dir:  ~/...' with fragile column alignment. 'ccp profile doctor' emits '[error] profile: message\n        hint: ...' that requires multi-line parsing. 'ccp version' emits a bare string with no key. 'sync status' has a multi-key columnar format. 'profile diff' uses prefix markers that conflict with standard unified-diff parsers. None have a --json flag.
findings.suggested_fix: Add 'var asJSON bool' + cmd.Flags().BoolVar(&asJSON, "json", false, "emit JSON") to each command, following the existing pattern in newProfileListCmd. For show: struct{Name,Active,SourceDir,RuntimeDir,Items[]}. For doctor: []struct{Profile,Severity,Message,Hint} (DoctorFinding is already the right shape). For diff: []struct{Kind,Path}. For sync status: StatusSummary already exists as a Go struct in internal/sync/sync.go — json.Marshal it directly. For version: struct{Version string}. For current: struct{Active string, Set bool} so agents can distinguish 'no active profile' (Set=false) from an empty-string profile name.

findings.title: sync pull has no --yes / non-interactive confirmation path; clean-tree check silently succeeds but dirty-tree check produces an error that looks like a user mistake
findings.detail: sync pull with a dirty working tree returns: 'working tree has uncommitted changes; commit them (ccp sync push), or re-run with --force to discard'. This is correct human guidance but conflates two agent-meaningful states: (a) there are local changes the agent should commit first (actionable: run sync push), and (b) the agent wants to discard local changes (actionable: re-run with --force). An agent cannot distinguish these from the error text alone without string-parsing. Also, --force has destructive semantics (discard + hard reset) that differ from a TTY-bypass --yes; agents may avoid --force by policy even when the intent is safe. There is no --yes that means 'I acknowledge the dirty tree but proceed with merge anyway'.
findings.suggested_fix: Split the flag into two with clear semantics: --force (existing: hard reset + pull) and an informational exit code for the dirty-but-safe case. When the tree is dirty and --force is absent, exit with a dedicated code (e.g. 5 = 'precondition not met, retry after sync push') so agents can branch without string-matching. Optionally add --dry-run to pull (symmetric with push --dry-run) so agents can preview what would change before committing.

findings.title: No ValidArgsFunction on profile-name arguments; shell completion and agent discovery are both broken
findings.command: ccp use / ccp profile use / show / delete / diff / rename / exec / doctor
findings.detail: Every command that accepts a profile name (use, show, delete, diff, rename, exec, doctor, refresh) uses cobra.ExactArgs or MaximumNArgs with no ValidArgsFunction registered. Cobra's dynamic completion framework calls ValidArgsFunction to populate tab completions for positional arguments. Without it, 'ccp use <TAB>' returns nothing, so both human users and agents that enumerate commands via --help + completion scripts cannot discover valid profile names without running 'ccp profile list' first. The List function and profile.List() already exist and could back a completion function trivially.

findings.title: ValidateName error message embeds a raw regexp; agents see the regex but not the human rule
findings.command: ccp profile create / rename (any name argument)
findings.detail: ValidateName returns: 'invalid profile name "Foo": must match ^[a-z][a-z0-9_-]{0,62}$'. An agent that submitted 'Foo' must parse a regexp to understand the correction, rather than reading a rule like 'must start with a lowercase letter, contain only lowercase letters, digits, hyphens, and underscores, and be at most 63 characters'. The regexp is also not self-documenting about the 63-character limit.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the regexp in the error with a prose rule: fmt.Errorf("invalid profile name %q: must start with a lowercase letter, contain only [a-z0-9_-], and be 1-63 characters (got %d)", name, len(name)). The regexp can remain for validation logic but should not appear in user-facing errors.

findings.title: ccp version emits a bare string with no --json; ccp current emits empty output (not an error) when no profile is active
findings.detail: 'ccp version' prints '0.1.0-dev\n' with no key. An agent composing a JSON report of tool versions must treat this as an opaque string and hope the format never changes. More critically, 'ccp current' exits 0 with empty stdout when no profile is set (profile_list.go:57-59). An agent running 'ccp current' and receiving empty output cannot tell whether ccp has no active profile, the manifest is missing, or the tool crashed with a swallowed error. There is also no stdout/stderr separation check for these commands — both write informational lines to stdout only, which is correct, but no audit-mode or quiet-mode exists to strip them.
findings.suggested_fix: For 'ccp current': exit 2 (or a named exit code) when no profile is active, so agents can distinguish 'active = work' from 'none set'. Alternatively add --json that emits {"active": null} vs {"active": "work"}. For 'ccp version': add --json that emits {"version": "0.1.0-dev"} — the Version variable is already ldflags-injectable (version.go:9), making this trivial to add with a BoolVar flag.

residual_risks.description: fslock.Acquire calls unix.Flock with LOCK_EX which blocks indefinitely. If a previous ccp invocation hangs or a test leaves a stale lock, agents will hang without timeout. There is no --lock-timeout flag or context-cancellation path.

sync status ChangedFiles list is populated by iterating a map (go-git's Status type is map[string]FileStatus), so the order of changed-file lines is non-deterministic across runs. Agents that diff consecutive sync status outputs may see spurious ordering changes.

ccp exec sets DisableFlagParsing: true on the Cobra command to forward flags to the child process unchanged. This means '--help' and '--version' passed before the profile name are forwarded rather than handled by ccp, silently running the child without ccp intervention. An agent calling 'ccp exec --help' receives child process help, not ccp exec help.

testing_gaps.description: No test exercises profile delete with stdin closed (i.e., io.EOF on first ReadString). The current tests likely only cover the --yes path. A CI test should run 'ccp profile delete name < /dev/null' and assert exit non-zero with an actionable error message, not exit 0 with 'Cancelled.'

No test asserts on exit codes for ErrNotFound vs ErrAlreadyExists scenarios. Adding sentinel-to-exit-code mapping has no regression surface unless tests call the real binary and check os.Exit codes (e.g., via exec.Cmd.ProcessState.ExitCode()).

sync status ChangedFiles ordering is untested for determinism. A test that creates two changed files and calls Status() twice should assert the slice order is stable (requiring a sort to be added to the implementation).
